solver.kind: blind AI solver B (separate agent, answer-free packet, adversarial rubric)

flags.note: Choice A/B call the narrator 'his'/'teenager...his'; the passage never states the narrator's gender. Harmless but an unsupported assumption repeated across the set (02, 03, 04, 08, 10).

R053-01.notes: A: no tournament win (grandfather once played in tournaments). C: no admission; ambiguity is never resolved. D: contradicted by final line asking to play again next week. B tracks bragging -> two unwelcome explanations -> unresolved.

R053-02.notes: 'Never let me win,' maxim plus taking the rook, narrator later repeats the lesson. B: he explains (the maxim). C: opposite. D: every Sunday. 'Strict' is fair; tissue adds warmth but does not make C viable.

R053-03.notes: 'Exactly the kind of move he had spent seven years teaching me never to make.' A reverses who loses the piece. D: narrator wins. B unsupported.

R053-04.notes: 'I decided to find out' -- a test of whether grandfather would see/take the queen. A tempting (he does end up losing gratefully) but the stated motive is to find out. 'Punish' = capture, acceptable chess idiom.

R053-05.notes: 'As plain as the unguarded queen' echoes 'a mistake so plain' -- obvious. Other senses don't fit.

R053-06.notes: Directly paraphrases 'could not tell whether his expression was kind or confused.' B and C use 'clearly,' which the text refutes. D unsupported.

R053-07.notes: Para 4 states two explanations; para 5 opens 'decided to find out.' A: first win was earlier (para 2). B, D unsupported.

flags.note: D credits the loss with letting him 'avoid learning an answer he feared'; strictly, it is his choice not to ask and to move the queen that avoids the answer. One could also read the loss as reassuring evidence that grandfather can still play. D remains the only defensible option and the 'keep their games going' half is well supported by the ending, so not blocking.

R053-08.notes: A: the loss proves nothing (he lost after rescuing his own queen). B: he lost. C: bragging never mentioned again. D best: question left unasked, games continue.

R053-09.notes: Echoes the grandfather's teaching and the weekly ritual, immediately followed by asking to play next week. B is a trap for students who think 'white on the right' is wrong (it is the standard light-square rule). C, D unsupported/contradicted.

flags.note: 'Grandson' assumes a gender the passage never states; no competing option, so not blocking. Retrospective framing ('looking back') is reasonably supported by past tense and 'the nine-year-old version of me.'

R053-10.notes: First person 'I' with 'my grandfather'; A, B, D clearly wrong.
